title: Will OpenAI file for an IPO during 2026?
resolution_criteria: This question will resolve as **Yes** if OpenAI, a parent company, or any subsidiary that is primarily responsible for developing ChatGPT, files a public, non-confidential initial public registration statement ([SEC Form S-1](https://www.investopedia.com/terms/s/sec-form-s-1.asp)) at the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission's [EDGAR](https://www.sec.gov/search-filings) database before January 1, 2027.
fine_print: If ChatGPT is renamed or is otherwise succeeded by a new model, the new model will qualify as "ChatGPT" for the purpose of this question.

comments.author: josheee
comments.text: At 27%, modestly below the community, mostly because of the resolution wording. It requires a public, non-confidential S-1 on EDGAR before 2027, and large tech issuers almost always file confidentially first under the JOBS Act, flipping to a public S-1 only about two to three weeks before the roadshow. So even a genuine, fully committed IPO process that kicks off in 2026 can easily see its public S-1 slip into 2027, which caps the yes probability below the market's read of "will OpenAI move toward an IPO." The 2025 for-profit/PBC restructuring did remove the structural blocker, but leadership has repeatedly downplayed a near-term listing and the company is still scaling losses, both of which argue against rushing a public filing this calendar year. I read the June-to-July drop in the community from the \~80s to the low 30s as the market repricing exactly this. The main paths to yes are a capital need that forces an accelerated public filing or a deliberate decision to file publicly rather than confidentially.
